clips.send: latitude 34.0°, 2026-11-21 at 19:46: full night (Sun -28°). The Moon is 91 percent lit and 53° up in the SE. Planets up: Saturn (SE 52°). About 5,000 real stars are on this map: every star down to magnitude 6, roughly what your eyes can see from a dark countryside. The whole sky turns 15° every hour (once in 23 h 56 min) because Earth spins from west to east. Planets always stay near the yellow dashed line, the ecliptic. It is the flat plane of the solar system seen edge-on. Each day the Moon moves about 13° east against the stars, so it rises about 50 minutes later each night. Stars twinkle; planets mostly shine steadily. If a bright “star” sits on the ecliptic and isn’t on a star chart, it’s a planet. Polaris is NOT the brightest star in the sky (it is about 48th). It is famous because it barely moves: it sits almost exactly above Earth’s North Pole.

The whole sky turns 15° every hour (once in 23 h 56 min) because Earth spins from west to east. Planets always stay near the yellow dashed line, the ecliptic. It is the flat plane of the solar system seen edge-on. Each day the Moon moves about 13° east against the stars, so it rises about 50 minutes later each night. Stars twinkle; planets mostly shine steadily. If a bright “star” sits on the ecliptic and isn’t on a star chart, it’s a planet. Polaris is NOT the brightest star in the sky (it is about 48th). It is famous because it barely moves: it sits almost exactly above Earth’s North Pole.

clips.send: latitude 34.0°, 2026-11-21 at 17:58: twilight, getting dark (Sun -6°). The Moon is 90 percent lit and 32° up in the E. Planets up: Saturn (SE 35°). About 5,000 real stars are on this map: every star down to magnitude 6, roughly what your eyes can see from a dark countryside. The whole sky turns 15° every hour (once in 23 h 56 min) because Earth spins from west to east. Planets always stay near the yellow dashed line, the ecliptic. It is the flat plane of the solar system seen edge-on. Each day the Moon moves about 13° east against the stars, so it rises about 50 minutes later each night. Stars twinkle; planets mostly shine steadily. If a bright “star” sits on the ecliptic and isn’t on a star chart, it’s a planet. Polaris is NOT the brightest star in the sky (it is about 48th). It is famous because it barely moves: it sits almost exactly above Earth’s North Pole.

clips.send: latitude 0.0°, 2026-11-21 at 21:00: full night (Sun -37°). The Moon is 91 percent lit and 70° up in the NE. Planets up: Saturn (NE 88°). About 5,000 real stars are on this map: every star down to magnitude 6, roughly what your eyes can see from a dark countryside. The whole sky turns 15° every hour (once in 23 h 56 min) because Earth spins from west to east. Planets always stay near the yellow dashed line, the ecliptic. It is the flat plane of the solar system seen edge-on. Each day the Moon moves about 13° east against the stars, so it rises about 50 minutes later each night. Stars twinkle; planets mostly shine steadily. If a bright “star” sits on the ecliptic and isn’t on a star chart, it’s a planet. Polaris is NOT the brightest star in the sky (it is about 48th). It is famous because it barely moves: it sits almost exactly above Earth’s North Pole.

The whole sky turns 15° every hour (once in 23 h 56 min) because Earth spins from west to east. Planets always stay near the yellow dashed line, the ecliptic. It is the flat plane of the solar system seen edge-on. Each day the Moon moves about 13° east against the stars, so it rises about 50 minutes later each night. Stars twinkle; planets mostly shine steadily. If a bright “star” sits on the ecliptic and isn’t on a star chart, it’s a planet. Polaris is NOT the brightest star in the sky (it is about 48th). It is famous because it barely moves: it sits almost exactly above Earth’s North Pole.

clips.send: 活动建议：（1）让学生用“现在”按钮生成今晚的星图，晚上到户外对照，记录看到的行星和月相；（2）连续一周每天同一时间观察月球，在星图上用 +1 天按钮验证它每天向东移动约 13 度 ；（3）把“夜空有多黑”滑块从城市调到乡村，讨论光污染，并参加 Globe at Night 公民科学项目。
